starProductsSummary: Six Maruti models in India's FY26 top 10 (Dzire #1, Ertiga #4, Swift #5, WagonR #7, Brezza #8, Baleno #10); 10 of top 25 in Aug-26 and 11 of top 25 in Sep-26. Volume engines: WagonR, Swift, Dzire, Alto, Eeco (Arena small cars, GST-2.0 beneficiaries). Profit/mix engines: Victoris, Grand Vitara, Fronx, Brezza, XL6, e Vitara (SUV/Nexa). H1FY27 UV volume +43.6% vs passenger cars +33.8%. Weak spots: Grand Vitara trails its own Toyota twin; Invicto 1,635 units H1FY27 vs Innova ~8-10k/month; S-Presso, Ignis, Celerio, Ciaz near-zero (Ignis & Ciaz 0 in Sep-26).

moatEvidence.evidence: Q1FY27 EBITDA margin: Maruti 8.6% (EBIT 5.1%) vs Hyundai Motor India ~9.25% vs Tata PV domestic 4.3% vs M&M standalone auto PBIT 7.1% (8.3% ex-eSUV contract mfg). Maruti's EBIT margin is BELOW M&M's auto PBIT and its EBITDA below Hyundai's. Scale has not given Maruti superior margins; the cost edge (localisation, scale) is largely passed to customers in low-priced small cars. Q1FY27 EBITDA/vehicle ~Rs63,100 (DERIVED: Rs43,111mn / 682,724).

Maruti 4,601 sales outlets (751 Nexa) and 5,926 service touchpoints (FY26) vs Hyundai 1,500+ outlets / 1,675 service touchpoints (May-2026) vs Tata PV 1,669 outlets / 1,211 service touchpoints (FY26; targeting 3,200/3,000+ by FY31). ~3x the nearest rival; 52% of FY26 sales non-urban; first-time buyers 54% in Q1FY27. M&M network count not found.

Autocar India-Spinny Used Car Study 2026 (transactions Jan-Aug 2025, 9 cities): Maruti best residual in MPVs (Ertiga), compact sedans (Dzire), premium hatch (Baleno, tied with Glanza), budget hatch (S-Presso). But NOT in SUVs: Tata Punch leads sub-compact SUVs, Kia Seltos mid-SUVs, M&M XUV700 executive SUVs; Hyundai Grand i10 Nios leads midsize hatch. Brand moat is strongest in cars, weakest where the market is growing.

Maruti ~4% of India EV sales H1 CY2026 (6,404 e Vitara; #4) vs Tata 39%, M&M 23%, JSW MG 21%. Domestic e Vitara allocation reportedly only 2,000-2,500/month with most output exported. Suzuki cut India BEV plan from 6 to 4 models by FY30. EV penetration hit 7.6% of PV retail in Aug-2026.

Maruti ~70% of factory-fitted CNG market; CNG ~40% of Maruti volume (Q1FY27), management targeting >9 lakh CNG units in FY27. Alt-fuels (CNG+hybrid+EV) overtook petrol in Aug-2026 (CNG 25% of PV retail). Strong hybrids so far rely on Toyota tech; in-house series hybrid (Fronx) has slipped from Q2FY27 to ~2027.

Improving at the top (new Dzire: India's first 5-star BNCAP sedan, Jun-2025; Victoris 5-star BNCAP 31.66/32 AOP), but legacy volume models lag: Wagon R scored 1-star adult / 0-star child in Global NCAP 2023 (19.69/34; driver chest 'weak'). Tata and M&M have built brand around 5-star ratings across lineups (Altroz, Harrier, XEV 9e 32/32). In 2014 Maruti's chairman defended a 0-star Swift by arguing car safety was not central to road fatalities.

Small cars: strong post-GST 2.0 (190k pending orders at FY26-end, ~130k small cars; network stock 3-4 days in Q3FY26). But in Q1FY27 Maruti could only take ~50bps price hikes (Jun + Aug) against ~300bps commodity hit - EBITDA fell 400bps YoY. SUVs: Oct-2026 Nexa discounts up to ~Rs1.36 lakh on Grand Vitara, Rs95k Invicto, Rs61k XL6 (vs Tata Nexon up to Rs75k, Curvv up to Rs1.25 lakh, M&M Thar 4WD Rs80k) - heavy discounting where Maruti is weak.

Maruti is ~49% of India PV exports in FY26 (~55% in Q1FY27); 447,774 export units FY26 (+35%); Japan supplied from India (Fronx/Jimny/e Vitara). Exports cushion domestic cyclicality, though Q2FY27 exports fell 2% YoY.

UVs ~68% of PV market; Maruti SUV share ~19.6% (FY26) vs ~79% in hatches. Sub-4m SUV share fell from ~30% (May-23) to ~26% (Q2 CY26) as Tata Punch/Nexon took #1/#2; Grand Vitara outsold by its Toyota twin Hyryder (78,140 vs 61,687 Jan-Sep 2026); Invicto 1,635 units in H1FY27 vs Innova ~8-10k/month.

critiques.point: Maruti's FY26 domestic share slipped to a 13-year low as buyers shifted to SUVs; M&M (14.2%) became No.2 and Tata ~13%, while Maruti still claims a 50% share target by FY31.
The H1FY27 share recovery (to ~41%) is driven by the GST 2.0 small-car tax cut - a one-time policy tailwind in a shrinking hatch segment, not a structural win in SUVs.
critiques.who: Analyst synthesis from AngelOne H1FY27 share data and Q1FY27 segment mix (mini +124%)

critiques.point: Wagon R - a top-5 car - got 1 star (adult) and 0 stars (child) in Global NCAP's 2023 test, with 'weak' driver chest protection.
Late and reluctant EV entrant: rivals Tata, JSW MG and M&M already locked in early adopters; Tata holds >40% EV share.
Cut near-term e Vitara production by about two-thirds (8,200 vs 26,500 planned for Apr-Sep 2025) due to Chinese rare-earth magnet curbs - exposes supply-chain dependence.
Suzuki scaled back its India EV ambitions to 4 BEVs by FY30 (from 6) and cut its long-term India volume outlook to 2.54mn units by FY30 from 3mn.
Q1FY27 operating margin collapsed to 5.1% EBIT (from 8.8% in Q4FY26) on aluminium/commodity costs and a supplier-settlement change; stock ~-22% from end-July to 52-week low by 22-Oct-2026.
Toyota alliance cannibalises: the Toyota-made Hyryder outsells Maruti's own Grand Vitara (13.0% vs 10.3% mid-SUV share Jan-Sep 2026) and Maruti's Invicto is a non-starter next to Innova Hycross.
critiques.who: Data from Autopunditz; Outlook Business noted Hyryder at times outselling its Maruti twin

critiques.point: Historic: CLSA cut Maruti to 'underperform' over SUV share loss and supply crisis (Dec-2021) - the SUV gap is a long-running thesis, not new.

Safety culture: after the basic Swift scored zero stars (2014), Maruti's chairman argued vehicle safety was not part of the safe-systems approach - a stance that still colours perception versus Tata/M&M.
Product slippage: in-house Fronx strong hybrid was reported for Q2 FY27 (Oct-2025) but latest reports put it in early 2027; Y17 3-row SUV timing has also drifted.
